correctness.rationale: Fixed independent directed-edge and fair-colour probability spaces; conditioning on concentrated class sizes gives n^{-1}e^{-t} hole probability. The mixed factorial moments explicitly control O(r^2) shared anchored edges and repeated witnesses, hence converge to those of \(2q^2\) independent Poisson(e^{-t}/q) variables. Deficient vertices have at most one missing flag with high probability; grouping by Boolean membership signatures gives the displayed binomial atom law. Closure under both union-preserving modalities is equivalent, with high probability, to zero deficiencies. Markov and conditional binomial estimates give both off-window sides. A standalone exact finite checker passes 4164 cases; infinite proof not inferred from tests.

value.rationale: The direct problem is whether a finite collection of propositional valuations generates further Boolean events through both future and past modalities. In the natural logarithmic edge-density window, the whole algebra is initially saturated with a nontrivial limiting probability, while a single modal step gains a binomial number of atoms. The theorem distinguishes vertex defects (independent Poisson) from definable Boolean signatures (binomial), characterizes the entire saturation probability at arbitrary modal depth and identifies the two threshold sides; it is neither a small arbitrary enumerative slice nor a mere fixed-p zero-one observation.
